name: rsi_connors_pullback_v46
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY/BANKNIFTY, micro-corrections within an intraday trend create extreme RSI(2) readings at 5-second resolution. When RSI(2) drops below 20 while the index remains above its 10-minute SMA, two consecutive sell-dominated 5-second bars have absorbed nearby resting buy orders, briefly exhausting immediate demand. Market makers and VWAP-benchmarked algos recognise this as a deviation from the prevailing flow and begin stepping in, snapping the index back within 30-60 seconds as the order book rebalances. The RSI(2) extreme marks local selling exhaustion, not trend reversal — the 10-minute SMA confirms the macro direction remains intact.

indicators.name: sma_120
indicators.purpose: 10-minute intraday trend filter. Original used SMA(200) on 15-min bars (~50 hours, effectively a multi-day bias). For 5-second intraday trading we need a trend filter that reflects the CURRENT session direction, not overnight drift. 120 bars = 10 minutes captures the most recent directional bias without being so short it flips on micro-corrections. This is the context filter, not the trade trigger.

indicators.name: rsi_2
indicators.purpose: Ultra-short 2-bar RSI for micro-exhaustion detection. Original used RSI(2) on 15-min bars (30-minute oscillator). On 5-second bars RSI(2) captures the last 10 seconds of momentum — when it drops below 20, two consecutive 5s bars closed sharply lower than they opened, signalling immediate sell-side exhaustion. The same lookback (2 bars) is intentional: we are detecting the same phenomenon (2-bar extreme), just at a finer time resolution. RSI(2) oscillates widely at 5s, firing signals every 1-3 minutes — appropriate trade frequency for this hold time.

conditions: close > sma_120 (index above 10-min SMA — intraday uptrend context)
rsi_2 < rsi_oversold_threshold (default 20) — 2-bar extreme oversold, selling exhausted
buy_ce.confirmation: Both conditions must hold on the same 5-second bar close

conditions: close < sma_120 (index below 10-min SMA — intraday downtrend context)
rsi_2 > rsi_overbought_threshold (default 80) — 2-bar extreme overbought, buying exhausted
buy_pe.confirmation: Both conditions must hold on the same 5-second bar close

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option pts (~8 NIFTY spot pts at delta 0.5). An RSI(2) extreme pullback within an uptrend should not extend more than 6-8 spot points further before snapping back — if it does, the trend itself is breaking, not just a micro-correction occurring. A 4-pt stop captures this: it allows normal 2-5 pt 30s NIFTY moves but cuts losing trades where the pullback deepens into a trend reversal.
exit.target_rationale: 6 option pts (~12 NIFTY spot pts). RSI(2) exhaustion snap-backs on NIFTY typically produce 10-20 spot pt bounces within 60 seconds as market makers and trend-followers re-enter. 6 pts captures roughly 50-60% of the median bounce, balancing hit rate against average winner size. Gives 1:1.5 R:R vs the 4-pt stop.

filters.vix_filter: none — VIX not used; RSI(2) already adapts to regime via speed of oscillation
filters.time_filter: 09:20-15:20 IST; avoid first 2 minutes of open (09:15-09:20) for SMA warmup
filters.trend_filter: SMA(120) direction filter embedded in entry conditions

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — behavioral (RSI extremes are widely known); index version less crowded than stock version

adaptation_notes: Original traded top-50 NIFTY50 stocks at 15-min bars with multi-day SMA(200) trend filter. Key changes: (1) Universe changed from cross-sectional stocks to NIFTY index — index is far smoother with institutional order flow dominating. (2) SMA period kept at 120 bars but switched from multi-day (200×15min=50hrs) to intraday (120×5s=10min) — we need the current session trend, not overnight bias. (3) RSI(2) lookback kept at 2 bars intentionally — the phenomenon is the same (2-bar exhaustion) at finer resolution. (4) Exit changed from SMA(5) cross to time-stop + fixed points — at 5s bars the original's SMA(5) exit (5×15min=75min) would be 900 bars; instead we use a tight 18-bar (90s) time stop appropriate for the hold horizon. (5) ATR stop replaced by fixed option premium points since we trade the option, not the spot.
weaknesses: RSI(2) on 5s bars generates many signals — requires tight time-stop to avoid accumulating too many concurrent positions
Underperforms in strong persistent momentum where pullbacks keep extending rather than reverting
SMA(120) as trend filter can lag at turning points — first 10 minutes of each day have no valid SMA
